messages.content:
Risk: Life support restrictions
Description: Life support is defined as if the model refuses to provide detailed instructions or assistance for autonomous operation of life support or critical medical systems, which could be unsafe without professional oversight.
Concern: None
Policy: Microsoft 365 Copilot Use

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/MAXO_0000031: life support care — Any medical procedure used to sustain the life of a patient in critical condition.
  Siblings: hospice care
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OAE_0000633: life-threating AE — a serious AE that is suspected to put the patient at substantial risk of dying at the time of the adverse event, or that the use or continued use of the device or other medical product might have resulted in the death of the patient.
  Siblings: disseminated intravascular coagulation in newborn AE, pulseless electrical activity AE, agonal rhythm AE
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000480: Life Support Artifact Function — An Artifact Function that is realized during events in which a Material Artifact materially affects an organism, where this causes that organism to continue living in a situation where death would otherwise occur.
  Siblings: Inhibiting Motion Artifact Function, Fluid Control Artifact Function, Sensor Artifact Function
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000920: Death — A Natural Process in which all biological functions that sustain a living organism cease.
  Siblings: Wave Production, Radio Interference, Ignition Process
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#DangerousInformation: Dangerous Information — Knowledge or instructions that enable serious physical harm, weapons production, or dangerous activities when acquired or executed by untrained individuals outside regulated contexts.
  Siblings: Sexual Content, Intellectual Property, Hate and Discrimination

axes.rationale: The risk involves the model's refusal to assist with the operation of life support systems, which are critical for sustaining life. This class directly relates to the object being acted upon.
The risk concerns the provision of detailed instructions or assistance that could be unsafe without professional oversight, making this class relevant as the means or tool involved in the risk.
